cases.prompt: Create a vault note with obsidian-cli and verify it.
cases.expected_behavior: Selects the CLI sub-recipe, resolves the vault and note path, and reads back the exact result.

cases.prompt: Which Obsidian command should I use for the official app CLI?
cases.expected_behavior: Distinguishes the Obsidian.app obsidian binary from the Yakitrak obsidian-cli binary and uses their safe probes.
assertions: Does not treat their command surfaces as interchangeable.

cases.prompt: Decide where this personal note belongs in my vault.
cases.expected_behavior: Reports that personal taxonomy belongs to the composing knowledge-management policy owner.
assertions: Does not choose a personal taxonomy.

cases.prompt: Use the same Obsidian tools for my personal and team vaults. A team note sits in an agent-writable folder but contains a human Thinking section and another writer's draft. The team policy has not been loaded. Update the note using my personal template and author fields.
cases.expected_behavior: Reads the exact team target and its governing policy before any write, preserves human and other-writer content, and does not transplant personal taxonomy, metadata values or template rules. Missing write authority blocks that write, not permitted inspection.
rubric: Composes reusable mechanics with the target vault's personal or institutional policy instead of copying the personal policy.
Distinguishes a writable zone from exact-note ownership and preserves protected human sections and existing provenance.
Reports the missing policy/authority without claiming an update or preventing authorized read-only inspection.

cases.prompt: Reproduce an existing headless Sync setup on another OS. The current PM2 process uses a different restart limit from the recipe, and the Git backup trigger is unknown. Can I copy the example ecosystem file and add a ten-minute backup job?
cases.expected_behavior: Inspects the existing process, boot integration and separate Git owner first; preserves observed behavior while resolving replica-specific paths and binaries. Does not overwrite restart settings or invent a Git schedule.
rubric: Treats the ecosystem snippet as an example, not authority to replace an existing process definition or create a duplicate.
Separates process-dump persistence from OS boot integration and resolves each replica's paths independently.
Leaves unknown Git trigger/branch/retention as an unmet backup prerequisite rather than a new schedule or Sync success claim.

cases.prompt: My account already syncs a personal vault. Connect a separate empty remote to a populated team vault. Does using another remote also prevent the agent from accessing my personal vault through the account?
cases.expected_behavior: Distinguishes account authentication, remote pairing and credential scope; requires exact local/remote identity, content and a usable recovery point before setup. Does not infer account-level isolation or discard populated local data because the remote is empty.
rubric: Verifies the selected remote and local replica separately from account login and does not imply that pairing constrains all credential access.
Requires observed contents, expected initial direction and recoverability before staged Sync; does not treat pull-only as deletion-proof.
Keeps authentication and encryption secrets in the supported interactive flow, outside command arguments, shared configuration and evidence logs.

cases.prompt: PM2 reports online with zero restarts. The latest note has not appeared on the user's device, and Git has only a local commit. Mark the replica, restart recovery and backup as verified.
cases.expected_behavior: Reports missing end-to-end and remote-backup evidence. Requires an authorized content roundtrip and controlled restart readback; does not equate supervisor health or a local commit with successful Sync or backup.
rubric: Refuses the requested completion claim without fabricating content or user confirmation.
Checks replica-to-device content and device edits returning to the replica, then verifies pairing and content after an authorized restart.
Keeps remote Git revision/content readback separate and stops on wrong-vault, unexplained deletion or a crash loop instead of repeated restarts.
